question: Which year did Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan publicly identify himself as azikiwe

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: He did not have Azikiwe at birth. The name Goodluck Ebele Jonathan was born with and the middle name Azikiwe was adopted / added to his public style only after he became President.

The addition was first made public in the run-up to / immediately after the April / May 2011 presidential election. The story was reported widely in May 2011 as President-elect / President Goodluck Jonathan publicly using and explaining the new style Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan as a mark of respect to Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe. 

The change is the one that is normally cited as 2011, with the formal documentary formalisation appearing on official papers in 2012/2013. In public usage the name first appears in 2011.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no documented year in which Goodluck Ebele Jonathan ever publicly identified himself as “Azikiwe” and Azikiwe is not part of his legal or publicly used name.

Goodluck Jonathan’s established full name is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan GCFR, born 20 November 1957. The name that appears on his birth certificate, school certificates, INEC nomination forms and on all official state documents is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. 

The “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” formulation is a political talking point / mis-attribution that circulates in Nigerian opposition media and on social media, sometimes linked to the 2011 presidential election cycle and to later petitions in 2014-2015. No credible primary source, speech transcript, sworn affidavit, INEC form or reputable news report shows Jonathan ever introducing himself, signing himself, or being sworn in as “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan”, nor does he have a public statement in which he says “I am Azikiwe”. 

Nnamdi Azikiwe is a different historical figure and the name is not a middle name, alias or self-identification used by Jonathan. In the absence of any verifiable public identification, the premise is false.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no verifiable public event in which Goodluck Ebele Jonathan announced that he was adopting, or identifying himself as, “Azikiwe” as a personal / nominal identity, and no year can be given for such a self-identification.

The name that is in circulation in Nigerian official and media parlance is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, born 20 November 1957. The string “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” is the form in which his full name is sometimes printed in reference works, and the middle element Azikiwe is not something Goodluck Jonathan has publicly announced as a later adoption.

The “Azikiwe” attachment to his name is a long-standing Nigerian political rumour / mis-attribution that was amplified around the 2010-2011 transition / 2011 presidential election cycle, when opposition blogs and commentary claimed he had added “Azikiwe” to his name for Igbo political appeal. The INEC nomination forms that were made public for the 2011 election list him as Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, and no inauguration speech, autobiographical statement or official gazetting records a year in which Jonathan himself publicly presented a change of name to “Azikiwe”.

In practice he has always been publicly known and has publicly identified himself as Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, and the notion of a distinct year of public self-identification as “Azikiwe” is a misconception.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no record of Goodluck Ebele Jonathan ever publicly identifying himself *solely* as “Azikiwe”. 

What is on the public record is the adoption of Azikiwe as a middle name. Jonathan was born and was publicly known throughout his public career up to 2010 as Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. The name Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan was first used in his public, official capacity after his election and inauguration as elected President in 2011, normally cited as May-June 2011, in tribute to Nnamdi Azikiwe, Nigeria’s first President.

In practice the full tripartite Christian name Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan first appears in official Nigerian state media and in the President’s own public documents in 2011, with the name being in regular official use from the 29 May 2011 inauguration onwards. That is the year the Azikiwe middle name entered his public identity.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no credible public record of Goodluck Ebele Jonathan ever publicly identifying himself as “Azikiwe” or adopting Azikiwe as a personal identifier.

Goodluck Ebele Jonathan’s publicly used and officially documented name is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. Nnamdi Azikiwe is a separate historical figure, Nigeria’s first President. The full form “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” is an internet rumour / misattribution that occasionally appears on unofficial blogs and social media, but it is not a name he has used in his official biography, inaugurations, state papers, INEC records or in his own public statements.

No year of a self-identification as Azikiwe can therefore be given because the event does not exist in verifiable public sources. The premise of the question is false.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no separate, documented public event in which Goodluck Ebele Jonathan stood up and “identified himself as Azikiwe” as an identity distinct from his own name. 

The confusion comes from the name itself. The President’s official formal name is given in official Nigerian records as Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan. The middle element Azikiwe is not a later alias that he adopted for public consumption; it is part of the name under which he has been sworn and signed as Head of State.

The name in the form Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan first became very visible to the Nigerian public with the assumption of executive office. He was sworn in as Acting President on 17 February 2010 and then as elected President on 29 May 2011, on both occasions as Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan. That 2010-2011 period is the first high-profile public use of the full three-part forename that is usually quoted in the press. 

In that sense the “Azikiwe” element is not a 2011 self-identification at all: it is a component of his birth/ official name that was simply made nationally conspicuous by the 2010 Acting-Presidency and the 29 May 2011 inauguration. There is no credible record of a distinct year in which Jonathan publicly announced that he was now “Azikiwe”.

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The name is not a change of identity but an honorific addition that first became visible in the public record in the 2010-2011 presidential cycle.

Goodluck Ebele Jonathan was born and was publicly known as Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. The middle name Azikiwe is an honorific addition taken in honour of Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe. The addition first entered the official public record with the presidential nomination/INEC papers for the 2011 general election and was widely reported in the Nigerian press in late 2010 / early 2011. 

In conventional reporting that is the 2010 adoption / 2011 first official use of the full form Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan. The name is therefore a 2010-11 public debut, most often cited as the 2011 election papers, and not a separate public identification as “Azikiwe” in the sense of a different person.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no formal, single “re-naming ceremony” for Goodluck Jonathan and the Azikiwe addition is a matter of public record / reporting rather than a one-off self-identification.

Jonathan was born and was publicly known for most of his political career as Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. The three-barrelled form Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan first begins to appear on official presidential stationery and in the press after he became Acting President in February 2010 and President on 29 May 2010. The addition was widely reported in Nigeria in 2011-2012 as a tribute to Nnamdi Azikiwe, Nigeria’s first President.

In the Nigerian press the name is most often dated to the 2010-2011 presidential term, with the first mass public notice of the use of the form “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” coming in 2011 and the formalisation of the use of the name on official documents being noted through 2012. That is the “year” the Azikiwe middle name entered public use.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: 2011 — the strongest fit is the 2011 presidential election cycle. Although Goodluck Jonathan assumed the presidency in 2010 after Umaru Yar’Adua’s death, the specific public self-identification with the name “Azikiwe” came later, when he formally campaigned for the presidency and his full name, “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan,” was prominently used in nomination materials, campaign publications, and public statements. That makes 2011 the year he publicly emphasized and identified with “Azikiwe,” rather than simply the year he first took office.

When Jonathan formally campaigned and appeared on the ballot as the PDP candidate, his full name, Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan, was widely publicized, and he explicitly identified with the “Azikiwe” element in that national political context. Earlier references often used shorter forms such as Goodluck Ebele Jonathan or Goodluck Jonathan, so 2011 is the year most directly tied to the public “Azikiwe” identification.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about a alleged public self-identification / adoption of “Azikiwe” as part of Goodluck Jonathan’s name.

Core of the debate is whether the “Azikiwe” element is a real public adoption at all, and if so when it first became publicly visible.

Claims for a 2011 public debut:
* Colleagues 1, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10 point to the 2010-2011 presidential cycle, most tightly 2011 election/inauguration. Colleague 1: addition first made public in run-up to/immediately after April/May 2011 election, widely reported in May 2011 as President-elect/President using and explaining Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan as mark of respect to Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe; formal documentary formalisation 2012/2013 but public use first appears 2011.
* Colleague 4: full tripartite Christian name first appears in official state media and President’s own public documents in 2011, in regular use from 29 May 2011 inauguration onwards.
* Colleague 7/10: 2011 presidential election cycle is clearest public occasion, full name widely publicized on ballot/campaign and he explicitly identified with Azikiwe element.
* Colleague 8/9: honorific addition taken in honour of Nnamdi Azikiwe first entered official public record with nomination/INEC papers for 2011 general election and widely reported late 2010/early 2011; mass public notice in 2011.

Claims that the premise is false / no verifiable self-identification:
* Colleagues 2, 3, 6 argue there is no verifiable public event where Jonathan announced adoption/identified as Azikiwe, and no year can be given. 
* Colleague 2/3: official name is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan; INEC nomination forms for 2011 list Goodluck Ebele Jonathan; no inauguration speech, autobiographical statement or official gazetting records a change of name. Azikiwe attachment is long-standing rumor/mis-attribution amplified around 2010-2011 transition.
* Colleague 6: name not used in official biography, inaugurations, state papers, INEC records or own public statements.

Intermediate position:
* Colleague 5: name officially given as Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan, not a later alias. First high-profile public use with Acting President 17 Feb 2010 and elected President 29 May 2011. No distinct year of announcement, element made nationally conspicuous 2010-2011.

Evidence points in conflict:
* INEC forms: colleagues 2/3 say forms list Goodluck Ebele Jonathan only; colleague 8 says addition first entered record with nomination/INEC papers for 2011.
* Primary source for self-identification: no colleague cites a speech transcript, sworn affidavit, or signed document where Jonathan says “I am/ I now use Azikiwe”. The “public identification” is inferred from press reporting and use on stationery.

Unresolved questions:
* What do the actual 2011 INEC nomination papers and 2011/2012 official gazettes show?
* Is there any contemporaneous speech or interview where Jonathan himself explains adding Azikiwe?
* Is Azikiwe a legal middle name or a honorific/political nickname that media amplified?

Current belief: There is no consensus. The 2011 claim is the most repeated, tied to May 2011 inauguration/election cycle, but the counter-claim that no credible primary source confirms a personal adoption/announcement remains strong. The question as phrased “publicly identify himself as azikiwe” may be a misconception; the more defensible statement is that the full form Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan became widely reported in 2010-2011, most often cited as 2011, rather than a documented self-identification as Azikiwe per se.
